## Classes

### <a name="proxmox_backup_server"></a>`proxmox_backup_server`

Writes a YAML file that the proxmox_backup_server providers read at runtime
to authenticate against the local PBS REST API. Declare this class on every
PBS node before declaring any pbs_* resources.

#### Examples

##### Configure providers for the local PBS API

```puppet
class { 'proxmox_backup_server':
  token_id     => 'root@pam!puppet',
  token_secret => Sensitive(lookup('pbs::token_secret')),
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `proxmox_backup_server` class:

* [`token_id`](#-proxmox_backup_server--token_id)
* [`token_secret`](#-proxmox_backup_server--token_secret)
* [`host`](#-proxmox_backup_server--host)
* [`port`](#-proxmox_backup_server--port)
* [`ssl_verify`](#-proxmox_backup_server--ssl_verify)
* [`ssl_ca_file`](#-proxmox_backup_server--ssl_ca_file)
* [`task_timeout`](#-proxmox_backup_server--task_timeout)
* [`config_file`](#-proxmox_backup_server--config_file)

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--token_id"></a>`token_id`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^@!\s]+@[^@!\s]+![^!\s]+\z/]`

API token ID (format: user@realm!tokenname, e.g. root@pam!puppet).

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--token_secret"></a>`token_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String]`

API token secret. Wrapped in Sensitive; never written to Puppet reports.

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--host"></a>`host`

Data type: `String`

PBS hostname or IP. Defaults to localhost (the PBS API on the same node).

Default value: `'localhost'`

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--port"></a>`port`

Data type: `Integer`

PBS API port. Defaults to 8007.

Default value: `8007`

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--ssl_verify"></a>`ssl_verify`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to verify the PBS TLS certificate.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--ssl_ca_file"></a>`ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A\//]]`

Absolute path to a CA certificate file when ssl_verify is true and PBS uses a private CA.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--task_timeout"></a>`task_timeout`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Seconds to wait for PBS background tasks (e.g. datastore creation) before
the providers give up. Defaults to 60 when unset.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-proxmox_backup_server--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\//]`

Absolute path where the transport config YAML is written.
A symlink is created at the provider discovery path when this differs.
Defaults to the agent's own confdir (fact `proxmox_backup_server_confdir`), which is where
the providers look; the compiling server's confdir may differ.

Default value: `"${$facts['proxmox_backup_server_confdir'].lest || { $settings::confdir }}/pbs_transport.yaml"`

## Resource types

### <a name="pbs_acl"></a>`pbs_acl`

The resource title is a composite of the three namevars joined by pipes:
`<acl_path>|<ugid>|<role>`, where

* `acl_path` is the object path the ACL applies to (e.g. `/` or `/datastore/backup1`),
* `ugid` is the user ID (`user@realm`) or API token authid (`user@realm!tokenname`)
  the ACL grants access to, and
* `role` is the PBS role to assign (e.g. `DatastoreBackup`).

Alternatively, provide only the path as the title and set `ugid` and `role`
as explicit attributes.

#### Examples

##### Grant a user backup access to a datastore

```puppet
pbs_acl { '/datastore/backup1|user@pbs|DatastoreBackup':
  ensure => present,
}
```

##### Grant an API token audit access to everything, without propagation

```puppet
pbs_acl { '/|automation@pbs!ci|Audit':
  ensure    => present,
  propagate => false,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_acl` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this ACL entry should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `propagate`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the ACL entry propagates to sub-paths.

Default value: `true`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_acl` type.

* [`acl_path`](#-pbs_acl--acl_path)
* [`role`](#-pbs_acl--role)
* [`ugid`](#-pbs_acl--ugid)

##### <a name="-pbs_acl--acl_path"></a>`acl_path`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\/[A-Za-z0-9._\-\/]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The ACL path (e.g. /, /datastore/local). Must start with "/" and may contain only letters, digits, ".", "_", "-", and
"/".

##### <a name="-pbs_acl--role"></a>`role`

namevar

Data type: `Enum['Admin', 'Audit', 'NoAccess', 'DatastoreAdmin', 'DatastoreReader', 'DatastoreBackup',
                      'DatastorePowerUser', 'DatastoreAudit', 'RemoteAudit', 'RemoteAdmin',
                      'RemoteSyncOperator', 'RemoteSyncPushOperator', 'RemoteDatastorePowerUser',
                      'RemoteDatastoreAdmin', 'TapeAudit', 'TapeAdmin', 'TapeOperator', 'TapeReader']`

The role to assign.

##### <a name="-pbs_acl--ugid"></a>`ugid`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^\s@!\/|]+@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(?:![A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The user ID (user@realm) or API token authid (user@realm!tokenname) this ACL applies to.

### <a name="pbs_api_token"></a>`pbs_api_token`

PBS returns a generated token secret only during creation. Set `secret_file` to
retain it on the Puppet agent without exposing it in reports or logs.

#### Examples

##### Create a token and retain its generated secret

```puppet
pbs_api_token { 'automation@pbs!ci':
  ensure      => present,
  enable      => true,
  comment     => 'CI automation',
  secret_file => '/etc/puppetlabs/puppet/pbs-ci-token.secret',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_api_token` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['comment']]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update. Only `comment` can be removed. Requires PBS 3.4 or later; older releases reject the parameter.

##### `enable`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether the token is enabled.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this API token should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `expire`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Expiry as a Unix timestamp. 0 or unset means no expiry.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_api_token` type.

* [`secret_file`](#-pbs_api_token--secret_file)
* [`tokenid`](#-pbs_api_token--tokenid)

##### <a name="-pbs_api_token--secret_file"></a>`secret_file`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Agent-local file receiving the one-time token secret on creation, written with mode 0600.

##### <a name="-pbs_api_token--tokenid"></a>`tokenid`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^\s@!\/]+@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+![A-Za-z0-9._-]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Full token ID in user@realm!tokenname format (e.g. automation@pbs!ci). The realm and token name may contain only
letters, digits, ".", "_", and "-".

### <a name="pbs_datastore"></a>`pbs_datastore`

Creates and updates datastore configuration entries. Note that `path` is
create-only: PBS does not allow moving an existing datastore, so changing
the path of an existing datastore raises an error. Delete and recreate the
datastore to change its location.

#### Examples

##### Datastore with daily garbage collection

```puppet
pbs_datastore { 'backup':
  ensure      => present,
  path        => '/mnt/backup',
  gc_schedule => 'daily',
  comment     => 'main store',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_datastore` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this datastore should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `gc_schedule`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Garbage collection schedule (PBS schedule string or cron format).

##### `path`

Data type: `String`

Absolute filesystem path on the PBS host. Create-only: PBS rejects path changes on existing datastores; delete and recreate the datastore to move it.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_datastore` type.

* [`name`](#-pbs_datastore--name)

##### <a name="-pbs_datastore--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,31}\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The datastore name (max 32 characters). Must start with an alphanumeric character or underscore, followed by
alphanumerics, ".", "_", or "-".

### <a name="pbs_node_config"></a>`pbs_node_config`

This resource is only meaningful for the local node: the resource title
must be the short hostname of the PBS host the transport talks to, and the
provider raises an error otherwise. The node configuration always exists
and cannot be deleted, so `ensure => absent` raises an error as well — to
stop managing these settings, simply remove the resource from the manifest.

#### Examples

##### Manage the node Notes and notification sender

```puppet
pbs_node_config { 'pbs':
  description => "# My PBS Server\\n\\nManaged by Puppet.",
  email_from  => 'pbs@example.com',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_node_config` type.

##### `consent_text`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Text shown on the login screen as a consent or banner message.

##### `default_lang`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Default web UI language (e.g. "en", "de").

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `description`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Free-form text shown in the Notes panel of the PBS web UI (supports Markdown). A single trailing newline is ignored when comparing state, since PBS strips it.

##### `email_from`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Sender email address used by PBS for outgoing notification emails.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Present keeps the configuration in sync. Absent raises an error (the node config always exists and cannot be deleted); remove the resource from the manifest to stop managing it.

Default value: `present`

##### `http_proxy`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

HTTP proxy used by PBS for outbound connections (e.g. https://proxy.example.com:3128).

##### `location`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Physical or logical location label for this PBS node.

##### `task_log_max_days`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Number of days to keep finished task logs.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_node_config` type.

* [`node`](#-pbs_node_config--node)

##### <a name="-pbs_node_config--node"></a>`node`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

PBS node name as returned by GET /nodes (the short hostname, e.g. "pbs"). Must be the short hostname of the local node.

### <a name="pbs_notification_matcher"></a>`pbs_notification_matcher`

Matchers route notifications to one or more notification targets based on
severity, calendar, and metadata field match rules. See `pbs_notification_target`
for managing the targets themselves.

#### Examples

##### Route errors and warnings to an SMTP target during business hours

```puppet
pbs_notification_matcher { 'business-hours-errors':
  ensure         => present,
  target         => ['smtp-relay'],
  match_severity => ['error', 'warning'],
  match_calendar => ['mon-fri 09:00-17:00'],
  mode           => 'all',
  comment        => 'notify ops during business hours',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_notification_matcher` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `disable`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Disable this matcher.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this notification matcher should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `invert_match`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Invert the overall match result.

##### `match_calendar`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Calendar schedule expressions to match (e.g. "mon-fri 09:00-17:00").

##### `match_field`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Metadata field matchers (e.g. "exact:type=gc", "regex:datastore=^backup-.*$").

##### `match_severity`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Severity levels to match. Valid values: info, notice, warning, error, unknown.

##### `mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum[all, any]]`

Whether all (AND) or any (OR) match rules must be satisfied. Defaults to all.

##### `target`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

Notification target names this matcher routes matched notifications to.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_notification_matcher` type.

* [`name`](#-pbs_notification_matcher--name)

##### <a name="-pbs_notification_matcher--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The matcher name. Must start with a letter, digit, or underscore and may contain only letters, digits, ".", "_", and
"-".

### <a name="pbs_notification_target"></a>`pbs_notification_target`

The `type` attribute selects the delivery mechanism and determines which of
the remaining attributes apply: sendmail/smtp targets use the mail-related
attributes, gotify targets use `server` and `token`, and webhook targets use
`url`, `http_method`, `body`, `header`, and `secret`.

#### Examples

##### An SMTP relay target

```puppet
pbs_notification_target { 'smtp-relay':
  ensure        => present,
  type          => 'smtp',
  server        => 'smtp.example.com',
  mode          => 'starttls',
  username      => 'pbs',
  smtp_password => Sensitive('secret'),
  from_address  => 'pbs@example.com',
  mailto        => ['ops@example.com'],
}
```

##### A webhook target

```puppet
pbs_notification_target { 'webhook-alerts':
  ensure      => present,
  type        => 'webhook',
  url         => 'https://hooks.example.com/notify',
  http_method => 'post',
  body        => '{"text": "{{ message }}"}',
  # header/secret values must be base64-encoded (PBS KeyAndBase64Val schema):
  header      => [{ 'name' => 'Content-Type', 'value' => 'YXBwbGljYXRpb24vanNvbg==' }],
  secret      => [{ 'name' => 'token', 'value' => 'aHVudGVyMg==' }],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_notification_target` type.

##### `author`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Author name shown in sent emails. Defaults to "Proxmox Backup Server (<hostname>)".

##### `body`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Webhook request body template (supports handlebars).

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `disable`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Disable this notification target.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this notification target should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `from_address`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

From address for sent emails. Required for smtp targets.

##### `header`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Hash]]`

        Webhook HTTP headers. Each entry is a hash with "name" and "value" keys, where
        the value MUST be base64-encoded (PBS KeyAndBase64Val schema), e.g.
        {'name' => 'X-Token', 'value' => 'c2VjcmV0'} for the plaintext 'secret'.
        Plaintext values are rejected by the PBS API or cause perpetual drift.

##### `http_method`

Data type: `Optional[Enum[post, put, get]]`

HTTP method for webhook requests. Defaults to post.

##### `mailto`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

List of email addresses to notify.

##### `mailto_user`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

List of PBS user IDs whose configured email addresses receive notifications.

##### `mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum[insecure, starttls, tls]]`

SMTP TLS mode. Defaults to tls.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

SMTP port. Defaults to 25 (insecure), 465 (tls), or 587 (starttls).

##### `secret`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[Array[Hash], Sensitive[Array[Hash]]]]`

        Webhook secrets available in templates. Each entry has a "name" and an optional "value", which
        MUST be base64-encoded (PBS KeyAndBase64Val schema), e.g.
        {'name' => 'token', 'value' => 'aHVudGVyMg=='} for the plaintext 'hunter2'. An entry given
        without a value keeps whatever PBS already stores. The API returns secret names but never
        their values, so drift is detected against /etc/proxmox-backup/notifications-priv.cfg, which
        requires the Puppet agent to run on the PBS node as root.

##### `server`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

SMTP relay hostname/IP (smtp) or Gotify server URL (gotify).

##### `smtp_password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

        SMTP authentication password. PBS never returns it, so drift is detected against the copy in
        /etc/proxmox-backup/notifications-priv.cfg, which requires the Puppet agent to run on the PBS
        node as root. Sent only when it differs from the stored value.

##### `token`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Gotify authentication token. PBS never returns it, so drift is detected against /etc/proxmox-backup/notifications-priv.cfg, which requires the agent to run on the PBS node as root.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum[sendmail, smtp, gotify, webhook]`

Target type. Determines the delivery mechanism. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `url`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Webhook URL. Required for webhook targets.

##### `username`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

SMTP authentication username.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_notification_target` type.

* [`name`](#-pbs_notification_target--name)

##### <a name="-pbs_notification_target--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The notification target name. Must start with a letter, digit, or underscore and may contain only letters, digits, ".",
"_", and "-".

### <a name="pbs_prune_job"></a>`pbs_prune_job`

Prune jobs periodically remove backup snapshots from a datastore according
to the configured keep-* retention options. Note that the schedule is set
via `job_schedule` (not `schedule`, which is a reserved Puppet metaparameter).

#### Examples

##### Daily prune keeping a week of dailies and a year of monthlies

```puppet
pbs_prune_job { 'prune-backup1-daily':
  ensure       => present,
  store        => 'backup1',
  job_schedule => 'daily',
  keep_last    => 3,
  keep_daily   => 7,
  keep_weekly  => 4,
  keep_monthly => 12,
  comment      => 'standard retention',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_prune_job` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this prune job should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `job_schedule`

Data type: `String`

        Prune schedule (PBS schedule string or cron format). Required by the PBS API.
        Maps to the PBS API field "schedule"; renamed here because "schedule" is a
        reserved Puppet metaparameter.

##### `keep_daily`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Keep one backup per day for N days.

##### `keep_hourly`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Keep one backup per hour for N hours.

##### `keep_last`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Keep the last N backups.

##### `keep_monthly`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Keep one backup per month for N months.

##### `keep_weekly`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Keep one backup per week for N weeks.

##### `keep_yearly`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Keep one backup per year for N years.

##### `ns`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Namespace within the datastore to prune.

##### `store`

Data type: `String`

Datastore name this prune job operates on.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_prune_job` type.

* [`id`](#-pbs_prune_job--id)

##### <a name="-pbs_prune_job--id"></a>`id`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Unique prune job ID. Must start with a letter, digit, or underscore and may contain only letters, digits, ".", "_", and
"-".

### <a name="pbs_realm"></a>`pbs_realm`

The `type` attribute selects the realm backend and determines which of the
remaining attributes apply:

* `ldap`: `server1`/`server2`, `port`, `bind_dn`/`bind_password`, `mode`, `verify`,
  `capath`, `filter`, `sync_defaults_options`, `sync_attributes`, `user_classes`,
  plus the LDAP-only `base_dn` (required) and `user_attr` (required).
* `ad`: the same LDAP/AD connection attributes as `ldap`, but `base_dn` is
  auto-detected and `user_attr` is not used.
* `openid`: `issuer_url` (required), `client_id` (required), `client_key`,
  `username_claim`, `autocreate`, `scopes`, `prompt`, `acr_values`, `audiences`.

#### Examples

##### An LDAP realm

```puppet
pbs_realm { 'corp-ldap':
  ensure        => present,
  type          => 'ldap',
  server1       => 'ldap.example.com',
  base_dn       => 'dc=example,dc=com',
  user_attr     => 'uid',
  bind_dn       => 'cn=search,dc=example,dc=com',
  bind_password => Sensitive('secret'),
  mode          => 'ldaps',
}
```

##### An OpenID Connect realm

```puppet
pbs_realm { 'sso':
  ensure         => present,
  type           => 'openid',
  issuer_url     => 'https://sso.example.com',
  client_id      => 'proxmox-backup',
  client_key     => Sensitive('oauth-secret'),
  username_claim => 'email',
  autocreate     => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_realm` type.

##### `acr_values`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Space-separated Authentication Context Class References.

##### `audiences`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Space-separated list of accepted token audiences.

##### `autocreate`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Automatically create PBS users on first successful OpenID login.

##### `base_dn`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Base DN for user searches. Required for ldap; auto-detected for ad.

##### `bind_dn`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

DN used to bind for searches (e.g. cn=search,dc=example,dc=com).

##### `bind_password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Password for the bind DN. PBS never returns it, so drift is detected against /etc/proxmox-backup/ldap_passwords.json, which requires the agent to run on the PBS node as root.

##### `capath`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

CA certificate or directory path for TLS verification.

##### `client_id`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OAuth2 client ID registered with the provider. Required for openid realms.

##### `client_key`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

OAuth2 client secret. PBS stores it in cleartext in domains.cfg and returns it over the API, so it is compared directly and needs no on-node access.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `default`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Set this realm as the default login realm.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this realm should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `filter`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP filter restricting which objects are considered users.

##### `issuer_url`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID provider issuer URL. Required for openid realms.

##### `mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ldap', 'ldap+starttls', 'ldaps']]`

Connection security mode. Defaults to ldap.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

LDAP/AD server port.

##### `prompt`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID prompt parameter (e.g. login, consent).

##### `scopes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Space-separated list of OAuth2 scopes to request.

##### `server1`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Primary LDAP/AD server hostname or IP. Required for ldap and ad realms.

##### `server2`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Fallback LDAP/AD server hostname or IP.

##### `sync_attributes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Attribute mapping for user sync (e.g. email=mail,firstname=givenName).

##### `sync_defaults_options`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Default options for realm sync (e.g. scope=subtree).

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['ldap', 'ad', 'openid']`

Realm type. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `user_attr`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP attribute that holds the username (e.g. uid, sAMAccountName). Required for ldap.

##### `user_classes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated LDAP object classes treated as user accounts.

##### `username_claim`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

JWT claim used as the PBS username (e.g. email, sub).

##### `verify`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Verify the server TLS certificate.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_realm` type.

* [`realm`](#-pbs_realm--realm)

##### <a name="-pbs_realm--realm"></a>`realm`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The realm identifier. Must start with a letter, digit, or underscore and may contain only letters, digits, ".", "_", and
"-".

### <a name="pbs_remote"></a>`pbs_remote`

Remotes are other PBS instances that sync jobs can pull from or push to.

The `password` is enforced. PBS never returns it over the API, so drift is
detected against the base64-encoded copy in /etc/proxmox-backup/remote.cfg,
which requires the Puppet agent to run on the PBS node as root. Changing
the password in the manifest rotates it on the next run; leaving it
unchanged sends nothing at all.

#### Examples

##### Remote authenticated with an API token

```puppet
pbs_remote { 'offsite-pbs':
  ensure      => present,
  host        => 'pbs.example.com',
  userid      => 'sync@pbs!puppet',
  password    => Sensitive('token-secret'),
  fingerprint => 'AA:BB:CC:...',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_remote` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this remote should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `fingerprint`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

TLS certificate fingerprint of the remote PBS server.

##### `host`

Data type: `String`

Hostname or IP of the remote PBS server.

##### `password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

        Password or token secret for the remote. PBS never returns it, so drift is detected against the
        base64-encoded copy in /etc/proxmox-backup/remote.cfg, which requires the Puppet agent to run
        on the PBS node as root. Sent only when it differs from the stored value. Not required when
        ensure => absent.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Port of the remote PBS API (default: 8007).

##### `use_node_proxy`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether to use the local node proxy for connections to the remote.

##### `userid`

Data type: `String`

The auth ID for authenticating to the remote PBS: a user ID (user@realm) or an API token ID (user@realm!tokenname). Maps to the PBS API field "auth-id".

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_remote` type.

* [`name`](#-pbs_remote--name)

##### <a name="-pbs_remote--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The remote name. Must start with an alphanumeric character or underscore, followed by alphanumerics, ".", "_", or "-".

### <a name="pbs_s3_endpoint"></a>`pbs_s3_endpoint`

Configures S3-compatible object storage endpoints under /config/s3.

The `secret_key` is required when creating an endpoint and is enforced
thereafter. PBS never returns it over the API, so drift is detected against
the plaintext copy in /etc/proxmox-backup/s3.cfg, which requires the Puppet
agent to run on the PBS node as root. Changing it in the manifest rotates
it on the next run.

#### Examples

##### Endpoint for an S3-compatible object store

```puppet
pbs_s3_endpoint { 'minio-local':
  ensure     => present,
  endpoint   => 'https://minio.example.com',
  access_key => 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE',
  secret_key => Sensitive('wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY'),
  path_style => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_s3_endpoint` type.

##### `access_key`

Data type: `String`

S3 access key ID.

##### `burst_in`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Inbound bandwidth burst allowance as a HumanByte string (e.g. "8 MiB") or a plain byte count string.

##### `burst_out`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Outbound bandwidth burst allowance as a HumanByte string (e.g. "8 MiB") or a plain byte count string.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `endpoint`

Data type: `String`

S3 server endpoint URL (e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com).

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this S3 endpoint should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `fingerprint`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

TLS certificate fingerprint for endpoint verification.

##### `path_style`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Use path-style S3 addressing instead of virtual-hosted-style.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Custom port for the S3 endpoint.

##### `provider_quirks`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Provider-specific compatibility adjustments.

##### `rate_in`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Inbound bandwidth rate limit as a HumanByte string (e.g. "8 MiB") or a plain byte count string.

##### `rate_out`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Outbound bandwidth rate limit as a HumanByte string (e.g. "8 MiB") or a plain byte count string.

##### `region`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

AWS/S3 region identifier.

##### `secret_key`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

        S3 secret access key. Required when creating the endpoint; not required for ensure => absent.
        PBS never returns it, so drift is detected against the plaintext copy in
        /etc/proxmox-backup/s3.cfg, which requires the Puppet agent to run on the PBS node as root.
        Sent only when it differs from the stored value.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_s3_endpoint` type.

* [`id`](#-pbs_s3_endpoint--id)

##### <a name="-pbs_s3_endpoint--id"></a>`id`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Unique S3 endpoint identifier. Must start with an alphanumeric character or underscore, followed by alphanumerics, ".",
"_", or "-".

### <a name="pbs_sync_job"></a>`pbs_sync_job`

Sync jobs transfer backup groups between datastores, either pulling from
(or pushing to) a configured remote, or locally between datastores on the
same PBS instance.

Note: the PBS API field `schedule` is exposed here as `job_schedule`,
because `schedule` is a reserved Puppet metaparameter and cannot be used
as an attribute name.

#### Examples

##### Nightly pull sync from a remote PBS

```puppet
pbs_sync_job { 'nightly-offsite':
  ensure       => present,
  store        => 'local',
  remote       => 'offsite-pbs',
  remote_store => 'backup',
  job_schedule => 'daily',
  group_filter => ['type:vm', 'group:vm/100'],
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_sync_job` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `encrypted_only`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Skip unencrypted backups during sync.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this sync job should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `group_filter`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

List of backup group filter expressions; only matching groups are synced (e.g. ['type:vm', 'group:vm/100']).

##### `job_schedule`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Sync schedule (PBS schedule string or cron format). Maps to the PBS API field "schedule", renamed because schedule is a Puppet metaparameter.

##### `max_depth`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Maximum namespace recursion depth (0 = no recursion).

##### `ns`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Local namespace to sync into.

##### `owner`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Auth ID that owns this sync job.

##### `rate_in`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Inbound bandwidth limit for pull jobs as a HumanByte string (e.g. "8 MiB") or a plain byte count string.

##### `remote`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Name of the remote configured on this PBS. Omit for local (remote-less) sync jobs.

##### `remote_ns`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Namespace on the remote datastore to sync from.

##### `remote_store`

Data type: `String`

Datastore name on the remote PBS.

##### `remove_vanished`

Data type: `Boolean`

Remove snapshots that no longer exist on the source.

##### `resync_corrupt`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Re-sync corrupted snapshots (pull jobs only).

##### `store`

Data type: `String`

Local datastore name to sync into.

##### `sync_direction`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['pull', 'push']]`

Direction of the sync job. Defaults to pull when omitted.

##### `transfer_last`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Transfer only the last N snapshots per group.

##### `verified_only`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Skip unverified snapshots during sync.

##### `worker_threads`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Number of parallel transfer threads.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_sync_job` type.

* [`id`](#-pbs_sync_job--id)

##### <a name="-pbs_sync_job--id"></a>`id`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Unique sync job ID. Must start with an alphanumeric character or underscore, followed by alphanumerics, ".", "_", or
"-".

### <a name="pbs_user"></a>`pbs_user`

Manages user accounts via the PBS access API. Password management is only
supported for users in the built-in `@pbs` realm and requires the Puppet
agent to run on the PBS host itself, because password hashes are verified
against and written to /etc/proxmox-backup/shadow.json locally.

#### Examples

##### User in the pbs realm with a managed password

```puppet
pbs_user { 'john@pbs':
  ensure   => present,
  comment  => 'John Doe',
  email    => 'john@example.com',
  password => Sensitive('correct horse battery staple'),
}
```

##### Token-only user that must not log in with a password

```puppet
pbs_user { 'backup@pbs':
  ensure         => present,
  password_login => false,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_user` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `email`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Email address of the user.

##### `enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the user account is enabled.

Default value: `true`

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this user should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `expire`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Account expiry time as a Unix timestamp (0 means no expiry).

##### `firstname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

First name of the user.

##### `lastname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Last name of the user.

##### `password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

        Write-only. Only supported for @pbs realm users, and requires the Puppet agent to run on the
        PBS host itself: it writes /etc/proxmox-backup/shadow.json locally. Set on create via the API.
        On update, written to shadow.json via yescrypt/libxcrypt. Drift is detected by verifying the
        hiera plaintext against the stored hash via crypt(3) — the password property triggers an update
        only when the stored hash no longer matches.

##### `password_login`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

        Whether the user can log in with a password at all, i.e. whether shadow.json holds a hash for it.
        `false` removes the hash, and removes it again if one is ever set (e.g. in the GUI), while the
        user and its API tokens stay; use it for token-only users. Disabling the user would disable its
        tokens too. `true` requires `password`. Unset (the default) leaves it unmanaged. Only supported
        for @pbs realm users, and requires the Puppet agent to run on the PBS host itself.
        Cannot be combined with `password => ...` when `false`.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_user` type.

* [`userid`](#-pbs_user--userid)

##### <a name="-pbs_user--userid"></a>`userid`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^\s@!\/]+@[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

The user ID in user@realm format. The user part must not contain whitespace, "@", "!", or "/".

### <a name="pbs_verification_job"></a>`pbs_verification_job`

Verification jobs periodically re-check the integrity of backup snapshots in
a datastore. Note that the schedule is set via `job_schedule` (not `schedule`,
which is a reserved Puppet metaparameter).

#### Examples

##### Weekly verification, re-verifying snapshots older than 30 days

```puppet
pbs_verification_job { 'verify-backup1-weekly':
  ensure          => present,
  store           => 'backup1',
  job_schedule    => 'sat 02:00',
  outdated_after  => 30,
  ignore_verified => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pbs_verification_job` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Optional human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PBS API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether this verification job should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### `ignore_verified`

Data type: `Boolean`

Skip snapshots that have already been verified.

##### `job_schedule`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

        Verification schedule (PBS schedule string or cron format).
        Maps to the PBS API field "schedule"; renamed here because "schedule" is a
        reserved Puppet metaparameter.

##### `outdated_after`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Re-verify snapshots older than N days.

##### `store`

Data type: `String`

Datastore name this verification job operates on.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pbs_verification_job` type.

* [`id`](#-pbs_verification_job--id)

##### <a name="-pbs_verification_job--id"></a>`id`

namevar

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\z/]`
_*this data type contains a regex that may not be accurately reflected in generated documentation_

Unique verification job ID. Must start with a letter, digit, or underscore and may contain only letters, digits, ".",
"_", and "-".

## Tasks

### <a name="pbs_api_request"></a>`pbs_api_request`

Call any Proxmox Backup Server API endpoint exposed by /api2/json.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `host`

Data type: `String[1]`

PBS host name or IP address.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 65535]]`

PBS API port.

##### `token_id`

Data type: `String[1]`

PBS API token ID, for example puppet@pbs!puppet-token.

##### `token_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String[1]]`

PBS API token secret.

##### `method`

Data type: `Enum['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE']`

HTTP method.

##### `path`

Data type: `Pattern[/^\//]`

API path below /api2/json, for example /version or /config/datastore/{name}.

##### `path_params`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, Any]]`

Path template values for placeholders such as {name}.

##### `query`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, Any]]`

Query string parameters.

##### `body`

Data type: `Optional[Hash[String, Any]]`

JSON request body parameters.

##### `ssl_verify`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Verify the PBS TLS certificate. Defaults to true.

##### `ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional CA bundle path.
